title: How to work a half cross-stitch
subtitle: Working a single diagonal leg to create a lighter texture
excerpt: A half cross-stitch is a single diagonal stitch that covers one square of the Aida fabric. It creates a lighter, open-weave texture than a full cross-stitch and is used in cross-stitch charts where a design calls for shading or a thinner fill. Most charts mark half-stitches with a triangle symbol rather than a filled square.
sourceNotes: Half cross-stitch technique. Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive. Standard guidance in major cross-stitch publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.
The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch.

content.text: A half cross-stitch is the lower-left to upper-right diagonal leg of a full cross-stitch worked without the crossing return. On
it covers one square with a single diagonal thread. Half-stitches create texture differences in a design: a half-stitch area reads lighter than a full-stitch area in the same colour.
Bring the needle up through hole 1 at the lower-left corner of the Aida square. This is the same starting point as a full cross-stitch.
Insert the needle down through hole 2 at the upper-right corner of the square. Pull the
snug but not tight. The single diagonal thread should lie flat against the Aida surface, not puckering or pulling the fabric.
Do not add the returning leg. The stitch is complete after the single diagonal. Move directly to the next half-stitch in the row.

Work all half-stitches in a section in the same direction: all lower-left to upper-right, not mixed. Mixed direction creates a visually uneven texture that reads as inconsistency in the finished piece.

End the thread the same way as full cross-stitch: weave the tail under at least four thread runs on the back. A short tail on a half-stitch area is more prone to pulling out because there are fewer adjacent thread runs to weave under.

items.symptom: The half-stitch area looks uneven compared to the full-stitch area in the same colour
items.cause: Some half-stitches were worked in the opposite direction to others.
items.fix: Unpick the inconsistently-directed half stitches and re-work them in the same direction as the others. All diagonals in one area should run the same way for a smooth result.

items.symptom: The single thread leg lies loosely and lifts away from the fabric
items.cause: The thread tension was too loose, or the strand count is too low for the fabric count.
items.fix: Pull the thread snug as each half-stitch is completed. On higher-count Aida (18-count or above), try one more strand to improve the coverage.

content.text: Half-stitches are also used as a base layer for tent stitch (also called petit point) in mixed-technique pieces. In most counted cross-stitch charts, half-stitches appear at the edges of a shape to soften the outline, or in shading areas where a full stitch would be too heavy. Reading the chart symbol key before stitching confirms which squares are half-stitches and which direction the chart intends.
